question: What makes the community health planning cycle a continuous process?

options.A: Staff members rotate through different departments every month
options.B: Evaluation findings feed back into a new assessment phase
options.C: The government mandates yearly structural overhauls of clinics
options.D: International donors require quarterly reports without interruption

explanation: The cycle is continuous because the results and lessons learned from evaluating a completed program directly inform the next assessment and planning phase. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: Why is community participation essential during health planning?

options.A: It removes the responsibility of data collection from nurses
options.B: It guarantees local acceptance and long-term program sustainability
options.C: It eliminates the need for any external funding or support
options.D: It speeds up the bureaucratic approval process in ministries

explanation: Involving community members ensures that the interventions match their actual lifestyle and values, making them more likely to support and sustain the program. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of a community needs assessment?

options.A: To punish health workers who fail to meet targets
options.B: To identify health status, resources, and environmental hazards
options.C: To increase the monthly revenue of local patent medicine vendors
options.D: To distribute free mosquito nets to every household

explanation: Needs assessment systematically gathers data on the community's health problems, available resources, and underlying risks before planning begins. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h2)

question: A community health nurse relies ONLY on clinic attendance records for a needs assessment. What is the major limitation of this approach?

options.A: It focuses too heavily on environmental sanitation and clean water
options.B: It misses vulnerable people who never visit formal health facilities
options.C: It takes too many months to compile all the statistical tables
options.D: It requires expensive computer software that clinics do not have

explanation: Clinic records only capture those who manage to reach the facility, completely ignoring sick individuals who stay home due to poverty, distance, or preference for traditional healers. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h2)

question: When setting health priorities, what does 'magnitude' refer to?

options.A: The geographical distance from the local government secretariat
options.B: The physical size of the primary healthcare center building
options.C: The financial cost of buying imported medical equipment
options.D: The total number of people affected by the condition

explanation: Magnitude measures the scale or prevalence of the health issue within the target population. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h3)

question: A community ranks a minor skin rash higher than a silent malnutrition crisis because the rash is visible. How should the nurse handle this discrepancy?

options.A: Address only the skin rash to keep political leaders happy
options.B: Ignore community input entirely and force them to address malnutrition
options.C: Abandon the planning cycle until the community changes its mind
options.D: Educate the community on hidden risks while respecting their local perspective

explanation: Balancing community concern with professional assessment requires health education so the population understands severe, hidden threats without feeling dismissed. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h3)

question: In the SMART criteria for objective setting, what does the letter 'M' stand for?
explanation: Measurable means the objective includes indicators that can be tracked and quantified during evaluation. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h4)

question: Which objective statement is correctly written for a community immunization campaign?

options.A: To make sure mothers bring their babies to the clinic whenever they are free
options.B: To improve the general health status of all infants living in the community
options.C: To immunize 80 percent of children under one year against measles within six months
options.D: To completely eliminate vaccine hesitancy across all households by next week

explanation: This statement is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound, unlike the other vague or unrealistic options. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h4)

question: What is resource mobilization in community health planning?

options.A: Storing excess vaccines in the central cold room indefinitely
options.B: Transferring clinical staff to urban hospitals without notice
options.C: Gathering financial, material, and human assets needed for activities
options.D: Ordering all medical supplies directly from foreign manufacturing plants

explanation: Resource mobilization encompasses identifying, securing, and organizing all types of assets required to run the health program. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h5)

question: How can a community health nurse address a shortage of professional staff during program implementation?

options.A: Reduce the operating hours of the health clinic to twice a month
options.B: Ask patients to pay double fees to hire private doctors from abroad
options.C: Utilize task shifting and train community volunteers for basic duties
options.D: Cancel the outreach program until the government posts new nurses

explanation: Task shifting involves delegating appropriate tasks to trained community health extension workers or volunteers, maximizing available human resources. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h5)

question: What is the primary focus of supportive supervision during implementation?

options.A: Replacing all local nurses with expatriate health specialists
options.B: Issuing formal query letters for minor documentation delays
options.C: Helping health workers stay motivated and follow clinical guidelines
options.D: Deducting salaries whenever community attendance drops slightly

explanation: Supportive supervision aims to guide, mentor, and assist field workers rather than simply fault-finding or punishing them. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h6)

question: A scheduled immunization outreach is blocked by heavy seasonal flooding on the primary road. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Cancel the entire health program until the dry season returns next year
options.B: Blame the community leaders for failing to pave the access roads
options.C: Adapt the plan by using alternative local transport or rescheduling promptly
options.D: Proceed through the deep floodwaters without life jackets or precautions

explanation: Implementation requires flexibility to troubleshoot unexpected environmental barriers without abandoning the intervention goals. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h6)

question: How does monitoring differ from evaluation in a health project?

options.A: Monitoring focuses on finances, while evaluation focuses entirely on physical buildings
options.B: Monitoring is done only by foreign donors, while evaluation is done by nurses
options.C: Monitoring occurs after project closure, while evaluation happens before planning
options.D: Monitoring is ongoing activity tracking, while evaluation is periodic impact assessment

explanation: Monitoring happens continuously during implementation to track progress, whereas evaluation assesses the final outcomes and long-term impact at specific milestones. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h7)

question: Why is it important to share evaluation results back with the community members?

options.A: It prevents community members from asking questions about the budget
options.B: It builds trust and empowers local stakeholders to sustain health gains
options.C: It satisfies the legal requirement to pay annual municipal taxes
options.D: It allows the nursing staff to take extended leave periods afterward

explanation: Sharing evaluation results ensures accountability and encourages the community to take pride and ownership in maintaining the health interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h7)

question: What is a common cause of flawed needs assessments in many primary health systems?

options.A: Strict adherence to international epidemiological guidelines
options.B: Inaccurate data and poor record-keeping practices
options.C: Excessive availability of high-tech medical laboratory computers
options.D: Too many community members volunteering to collect surveys

explanation: Inconsistent or poorly managed health records often distort baseline data, leading to inaccurate community diagnoses. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h8)

question: How can community health nurses protect health plans from sudden shifts in government political priorities?

options.A: Keep all health program documents secret from elected government officials
options.B: Stop conducting community outreach until elections are completely abolished
options.C: Rely exclusively on foreign loans that bypass local political offices
options.D: Engage traditional rulers and local leaders for stable, long-term backing

explanation: Traditional and community leaders remain stable fixtures in the community across different political regimes, ensuring project continuity. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h8)
